title: Step 3: products for each part
objectives: Choose suitable products for each part of the mix.
Name what to watch for in each part.
body_md:
Step three is the product choice, and it comes last for a reason.

## The parts and their products

| Part of the mix | Suitable options | Watch for |
|---|---|---|
| Core equity | Flexi-cap, large-cap or index funds | Overlap between funds |
| Satellite equity | Mid-cap, small-cap, thematic funds | Keep small; higher risk |
| Debt | Short-duration, corporate bond, gilt, target-maturity funds | Credit and interest-rate risk |
| Gold | Gold ETFs or gold funds | Usually 5–15% is enough |
| All-in-one | Multi-asset, balanced advantage, aggressive or conservative hybrid funds | Check the actual mix in the factsheet |

## Two rules

- Match the product's risk-o-meter to the client's profile; do not put a small-cap fund in a three-year pot.
- Check overlap. Five flexi-cap funds are one holding with five expense ratios.

## The test

Before any product is named, the mix, the horizon and the risk profile are already agreed. If the product is driving the conversation, the order is wrong.
example: For a 60/30/10 mix: a flexi-cap fund plus an index fund for the equity core, a short-duration fund and a target-maturity fund for debt, and a gold ETF for the 10% — each checked against the risk-o-meter.
say: We'll match each product to the part of the mix it fills, and check the risk-o-meter.
Satellite holdings stay small, because their risk is higher.
never: This new fund is excellent; let's build the plan around it.
Small-cap funds are fine for a three-year goal.

talk_track.title: Step 3: choose products for each part
talk_track.text: Step three: choose products for each part of the mix. For core equity: flexi-cap, large-cap or index funds; watch for overlap between funds. For satellite equity: mid-cap, small-cap or thematic funds; keep this part small. For debt: short-duration, corporate bond, gilt or target-maturity funds; watch credit and interest-rate risk. For gold: gold ETFs or gold funds; five to fifteen percent is usually enough.

check.q: Which is a core equity holding?
check.why: The core is broad: flexi-cap, large-cap or index funds. Satellites such as mid-cap, small-cap and thematic funds stay small.

check.q: What should you watch for in the debt part?
check.why: Debt carries credit and interest-rate risk, as covered in Module 6. It is not risk-free.

check.q: How much gold is usually enough?
check.why: Gold is a diversifier: usually 5–15% is enough, and it can be flat for long periods.
